# Styles

Airbus Design System CSS API

## Introduction

This package implements CSS classes based on the Airbus Design System : [https://design-system.airbus.corp/](https://design-system.airbus.corp/) (goto/design-system)

User documentation can be found here : https://css.design-system.airbus.corp/

It is also used by the Design System react and angular components internally.

## 3rd party licenses

Dev Dependencies of this package are used only for development and build purposes, and are not included in the final output.

Projects consuming this package do not have to include them, and are not subject to their licenses.

For projects importing this package, the following 3rd party licenses apply:

## Approach

The approach is based on [CSSinJS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSS-in-JS) philosophy where we use Typescript to describe styles in a declarative way.

These declarations are used at compilation time to generate static stylesheets, or at runtime to generate dynamic styles (through the [JSS framework](https://cssinjs.org/?v=v10.5.0) for React).

Each module export what we call "Style Functions". This functions take the theme object as a parameter, and return a Style definition object, directly usable by the JSS framework, at buildtime or at runtime.

### Class names conventions

Style functions must return an object with some naming conventions.

* **root**: main class
* **_***: modifier class corresponding to a state (eg. variant, size, etc.)
* **camelCase identifier**: for childs (eg. Remove Button of the Banner)

For example here is the structure of the Banner style function, and the corresponding compiled classes in the comments.

```js
export const Banner = (theme: any) => {
  return {
    root: {               // .ds-banner
      "&:before": {}      // .ds-banner:before
    },
    _warning: {           // .ds-banner--warning
      "&:before": {},     // .ds-banner--warning:before
      "& $removeBtn": {}, // .ds-banner--warning .ds-banner-remove-btn
    },
    removeBtn: {          // .ds-banner-remove-btn
      "&:hover": {},      // .ds-banner-remove-btn:hover
    },
  };
};
```

### JSS Syntax

The syntax supported by the JSS framework is documented here : https://cssinjs.org/jss-syntax

We use [jss-preset-default](https://cssinjs.org/jss-preset-default) that provide the following plugins

* [Camel case syntax](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-camel-case)
* [Default units for numeric values](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-default-unit)
* [Rule value function](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-rule-value-function)
* [Rule value observable](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-rule-value-observable)
* [String templates](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-template)
* [Global selectors](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-global)
* [Extending styles](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-extend)
* [Pseudo and Nested Selectors](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-nested)
* [Classes composition](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-compose)
* [Vendor prefixes](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-vendor-prefixer)
* [Props sort](https://cssinjs.org/jss-plugin-props-sort)

## Build

Building the CSS library

```bash
npm run build
```

Building the documentation

```bash
npm run build-storybook
```
